title: A stack machine

milestone.title: From Machine Code to Modern Languages

description:
Run bytecode on a small virtual machine, the way Python and Java do.

```
PUSH 2
PUSH 3
ADD
PUSH 4
MUL
PRINT
-> 20
```

starter.main.py:
program = """PUSH 2
PUSH 3
ADD
PUSH 4
MUL
PRINT"""

stack = []
for number, line in enumerate(program.splitlines(), start=1):

hints: For `SUB`, pop `b` first and then `a`, and push `a - b`: the order matters (lesson 5.03).
Add `JUMP n` and `JUMPZ n` (jump if the top is zero) to make loops; the loop then needs an index instead of `for`.
requirements: A list is the stack; each instruction pops its inputs and pushes its result.
Popping an empty stack prints `stack underflow at line n` and stops.
stretch: Write a program for your machine that counts down from 5.
